summary: Python framework for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, clients and apps: turn a Python function into a tool an LLM can call.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: FastMCP is a framework for the Model Context Protocol, the standard that connects LLMs to tools and data. You write ordinary Python functions, mark them as tools, and FastMCP generates the schema, validation and docs. It also provides clients that connect to MCP servers and handle transports, authentication and the protocol lifecycle, plus apps that give tools interactive UIs inside the conversation.
sixtySeconds.problem: Writing an MCP server by hand means dealing with schemas, transports and auth. FastMCP hides that so a working server is a few lines of Python.
whoFor: Python developers exposing tools to AI assistants
Teams building MCP servers for internal data
Developers connecting apps to MCP servers
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the most widely used MCP framework, with servers, clients and apps in one package and an official install guide.

overview: Add FastMCP to your project with uv add fastmcp. The full installation guide (including verification and upgrading) is at gofastmcp.com.
A server is a FastMCP object with functions decorated as tools; calling mcp.run() starts it. Resources and prompts can be exposed the same way.

FastMCP 1.0 was folded into the official MCP Python SDK in 2024, and this standalone project continues it. Upgrade guides cover moves from earlier FastMCP and MCP SDK versions. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

steps.title: Create the server
steps.body: from fastmcp import FastMCP, then mcp = FastMCP("Demo").

steps.title: Add a tool
steps.body: Decorate def add(a: int, b: int) -> int with @mcp.tool and return a + b.
